source.title: Measuring Structure Development in Algorithmic Transformers

record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments on algorithmic sorting and circuit structure, but does not test grokking or the delayed-generalization behavior in any listed claim version. It mentions modular-addition grokking in related work.
record.gate_note: The post measures learning-coefficient and circuit-structure changes during sorting and cumulative-sum training. Those results do not measure a train/test generalization gap, a grokking jump, or the proposed grokking mechanisms. Rows below record relevant algorithmic-training findings under versions none.
record.test_reason: The post tracks LLC, rank, translational symmetry and head overlap in sorting and cumulative-sum transformers. It reports no train/test gap, no delayed generalization, no training-set-size sweep and no memorizing-vs-generalizing split. Grokking appears only as a related-work citation (Panickssery and Vaintrob, modular addition). Its structural changes after accuracy saturates are a related but different construct from any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the LLC drop coincides with head specialization in sorting transformers, without conclusive evidence that specialization causes it. They add caveats: the LLC misses the state/anti-state transition under noisy data and the late crystallization. They also find matrix rank an unreliable complexity proxy, and the LLC drop size not proportional to specialization.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use sorting and cumulative-sum tasks and track LLC and circuit structure, rather than testing the original modular-addition grokking setup or its delayed generalization behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer norm, weight decay, training-data perturbation, vocabulary size, list length, and number of heads change the reported LLC or circuit-structure dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: In sorting transformers, LLC and circuit structure keep changing after reported accuracy has reached its maximum. The form of these changes depends on layer norm, weight decay, data noise and head count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Algorithmic transformers undergo substantial structural simplification during training even after task accuracy saturates.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing vocabulary size or list length changes the number or size of vocabulary regions in the learned OV circuits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The vocabulary-region organization of sorting circuits depends on task dimensions.

fits_no_version.finding: For cumulative sum, the LLC rises and plateaus as accuracy reaches 100%, with no reported circuit simplification.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLC and structural dynamics differ across algorithmic tasks.

record.problems: Accuracy is not consistently identified as training, validation, or test accuracy. Numerical outcomes are mostly qualitative statements, with several figure-based plots but no reported uncertainty estimates. The post says the authors lack conclusive evidence that head specialization causes the LLC drop.
record.rows_left_out: No results relevant to algorithmic training dynamics were left out.

untested.parts: No held-out test accuracy versus train accuracy, no delayed jump from chance, and no dataset-size dependence. The accuracy type is mostly unspecified, and training data is sampled fresh rather than drawn from a small fixed set.
No generalization jump for progress measures to anticipate. The LLC and circuit measures track structure after accuracy saturates, not before a test-accuracy rise.
No non-algorithmic data, and no initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep tied to delayed generalization.
Weight decay is ablated, but only its effect on circuit cleanliness is reported. Nothing on critical dataset size, ungrokking, or generalization timing.
Head counts and regularization vary and give different circuit organizations, but only on sorting, without grokking, and without a comparison of independent seeds.
No test of optimizer or floating-point artifacts as causes of delayed generalization.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions none. No accuracy row distinguishes train from held-out data, except the noisy-data run, which is evaluated on a non-noisy validation set. The no-layer-norm run's slow rise to about 90% (r6) is not described as a train/test gap, so it is not evidence for V1.

versions.untested_parts: No train/test accuracy comparison, chance-level test performance, delayed test-accuracy rise, or training-set-size sweep.
No separation of generalizing and memorizing components, and no test of whether a progress measure anticipates a generalization jump.
No non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/weight-norm sweep testing grokking-like delays.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
No test of an efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No comparison of whether independent runs converge to the same algorithm.
No test of adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts as causes of grokking.

rows.subject: 3-head attention model
rows.operation_detail: Tracked LLC and OV-circuit head roles during sorting training
rows.baseline: At peak LLC, all three heads divide vocabulary regions
rows.value: As LLC drops, head 2 takes over the range handled by head 3; head 3 becomes an anti-state approximately negatively proportional to the sum of the other heads' OV circuits
rows.note: The post presents this as a change in learned circuit organization.

rows.subject: 4-head attention model
rows.operation_detail: Tracked LLC and OV-circuit head roles during sorting training
rows.value: Around training step 5000, head 2 settles into an anti-state as the LLC sharply drops; around step 100k, head 3 settles into a state similar to the 1-head sorting solution as the LLC drops slightly
rows.note: The post also says heads 1 and 4 specialize by splitting the dictionary.

rows.subject: cumulative sum algorithmic transformer
rows.operation_detail: Tracked LLC and accuracy during cumulative-sum training
rows.value: LLC goes up and plateaus as accuracy reaches 100%
rows.note: The post reports no circuit simplification and says the model goes directly to its final structure.
